column1: # 0008: "The audit must classify every ivar reachable from the selected roots
# as a stored field, immutable prepared value, eliminated reference-only trace
# field, or Full-only value with a reason."
# MOST OF THAT IS DERIVED, not written here. The reader's own type for the
# storage settles it: `int` and `bool` are stored scalars, `int_array` is a
# stored array, `string` and `str_array` are prepared byte resources, and an
# `obj_*` is a reference to something Full owns, which CORE cannot hold at all.
# This table is only for the fields whose type the reader left `poly` or
# `poly_array` -- it resolved the expression but not what it produces -- and a
# field in that state with no row here fails the audit.

column4: A 16.16 slope bound for aiming. Fixed point is an integer here.
The other end of the same aiming range.
A 0/1 flag, stored numerically per 0008 and compared explicitly.
A mobj slot index, or -1 for none. The negative is the sentinel, which is why it is i64 and not u32.
A mobj slot index, same shape as linetarget.
Player health. Goes negative on death in vanilla, so the domain includes it.
Per-floor crush flags, one element per moving floor. An array of 0/1.
Column span end, a screen row.
Column span start, a screen row.
An OFFSET into the texture atlas, not an address. CORE has no addresses; Full owns the atlas and CORE indexes it.
The second half of the same offset pair.

The fuzz table index, 0..49 (render.rb:454, 1990, 2016-2017). Typed poly since upstream stopped calling `poly - poly` an int: `count = yh - yl` reads @dc_yl / @dc_yh, which the reader leaves poly; the values are column numbers.

A flag, false or true (specials.rb:430, 471), stored numerically per 0008. Typed poly on the new pin because it is first written in change_sector, not initialize, so it is nil until then; its one read (specials.rb:443) follows the write at 430 in the same method.

Line numbers whose special is 48 (specials.rb:63 stores `i`, an int). Typed poly_array on the new pin because an array ivar written in an included module (Specials, in Game) loses its element type there; a plain class keeps int_array.
ANIMDEFS row[0], 0 or 1 (texture.rb:183). ANIMDEFS mixes integers and names, so a row's element is poly; columns 0 and 3 are integers.
A texture or flat number from texture_num / flat_num (texture.rb:184).
ANIMDEFS row[3], the cycle speed in tics (texture.rb:186).

`@sbar = wad.num_for_name("STBAR")` at statusbar.rb:111 -- a LUMP NUMBER, not the patch's bytes. Measured by reading it off a StatusBar built from doom1.wad; calling it u8 made the reference route refuse it as a value outside a byte, which is what said so.
`wad.num_for_name("STARMS")` at statusbar.rb:156 -- a lump number, same as @sbar.
`wad.num_for_name("STTPRCNT")` at statusbar.rb:112 -- a lump number, same as @sbar.
The WAD directory: an array of Lump objects. CORE receives buffers, not object references, and what it needs from a lump -- a position and a size -- Full passes as scalars or prepares as a table.
The flat number that means sky. Full resolves it when it loads the map and the closure only reads it, so it is a prepared value and not storage CORE keeps.
The sky texture index, resolved by Full at map load and only read here.
The REJECT lump: one bit per sector pair, prepared by Full and read by the sight check. Bytes, not a number.

Reference-only random trace. Allocated only by Random#trace!(cap), which only bin/sim_demo.rb calls (its rand.tsv differential oracle); bin/doom.rb never enables it, and the CORE port examples/doom/core/src/random.rb has no trace. The original and sim_demo are unchanged.
The trace's fill count, read and written only under `if @trace` in p_random and by sim_demo's log_n reader.
The trace switch: false unless trace! is called; it guards only the trace writes.
Set by Random#tic= and read only into @log_tic; the port's draws do not take it.
